answer:
ALiBi adds a head-specific negative slope times query-key distance before softmax. A separate causal restriction excludes future keys; a distance bias alone is not a causal mask. The supplied slope schedule handles non-power-of-two head counts. Cached blocks use absolute query offsets. Different slopes give different distance preferences, but extrapolation quality still needs evaluation at the target context length.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For causal positions $j\le i$, use $s_{hij}=q_{hi}^Tk_{hj}/\sqrt{d_h}-m_h(i-j)$. Positive slope $m_h$ penalizes distant keys; future keys remain separately forbidden. The bias is added before normalization, so its effect depends jointly on content scores and relative position, not on a post-softmax distance multiplier. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://docs.mosaicml.com/projects/composer/en/v0.3.0/method_cards/alibi.html) and [2](https://nn.labml.ai/transformers/alibi/index.html).
